# Lisbon Budget Trip Snapshot

A relaxed 5-day plan for 2 adults in Lisbon from **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-14**, keeping the trip under **€1,800 total excluding flights**.
Designed around **walkable historic areas, one museum max per day, seafood meals, one day trip outside the city, and a safe central base with easy transit**.

# 5-Day Lisbon Itinerary With Estimated Costs

| Day | Focus | Transit Plan | Est. Cost for 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apr 10 | Baixa, Chiado, Alfama | Airport transfer + walk + tram/elevator | €210 |
| Apr 11 | Belém + riverside | Tram/train + walking | €220 |
| Apr 12 | Day trip to Sintra | Train + local bus/taxi + walking | €260 |
| Apr 13 | Bairro Alto, Príncipe Real, Cais do Sodré | Metro + walking + tram | €205 |
| Apr 14 | Mouraria, Graça, final stroll | Walk + metro/airport transfer | €175 |

## Day 1: Old Lisbon Welcome
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

- Morning: Arrive, check in to a central stay in **Baixa/Chiado, Rossio, or Avenida da Liberdade** for safety and transit convenience.
- Afternoon: Easy walk through **Baixa, Rossio, Rua Augusta, and Chiado**; keep the pace light after travel.
- Evening: Sunset in **Alfama** with a simple seafood dinner, such as grilled sardines or arroz de marisco.
- Transit: Use an **airport transfer or metro** into the center; then stay on foot.
- Estimated cost: **€210**
  - Lodging: €130
  - Food: €55
  - Transit: €25

## Day 2: Belém and the Riverfront
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

- Morning: Visit **Jerónimos Monastery** or **MAAT**; choose only one museum/monument stop to keep the day relaxed.
- Afternoon: Walk the riverside, stop at **Belém Tower exterior**, and take a pastel de nata break.
- Evening: Seafood dinner back in the center, ideally in **Cais do Sodré** or **Chiado**.
- Transit: **Tram 15E** or a train/walk combo from central Lisbon.
- Estimated cost: **€220**
  - Lodging: €130
  - Food: €60
  - Transit/entry: €30

## Day 3: Sintra Day Trip
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/train-front.svg

- Morning: Take the **train from Rossio to Sintra** early to avoid crowds.
- Afternoon: Focus on **one major site only** — either **Pena Palace** or **Quinta da Regaleira** — then leave room for a slow lunch and village stroll.
- Evening: Return to Lisbon and keep dinner simple near your hotel.
- Transit: **Train + local bus or taxi** in Sintra; avoid trying to see too much.
- Estimated cost: **€260**
  - Lodging: €130
  - Food: €55
  - Transit/entry: €75

## Day 4: Viewpoints and Food-Forward Neighborhoods
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

- Morning: Wander **Mouraria** and **Graça** for viewpoints and quiet historic streets.
- Afternoon: Browse **Príncipe Real** and nearby gardens; optional light museum stop if you want one, but this day works well without one.
- Evening: Dinner in **Cais do Sodré** or **Bairro Alto** with seafood and a calm wine bar afterward.
- Transit: Mostly **walking**, with **metro** only if needed for hills or fatigue.
- Estimated cost: **€205**
  - Lodging: €130
  - Food: €60
  - Transit/extra: €15

## Day 5: Easy Final Morning
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg

- Morning: Last slow walk through **Alfama** or along the river; pick up souvenirs and coffee.
- Afternoon: Late lunch before departure; if time allows, do one final viewpoint rather than a full attraction.
- Evening: Airport transfer and departure.
- Transit: **Metro or pre-booked transfer** depending on flight time.
- Estimated cost: **€175**
  - Lodging: €130
  - Food: €35
  - Transit: €10

# Budget Breakdown and Stay Strategy

| Category | Estimated Total |
|---|---:|
| Lodging, 4 nights | €520 |
| Food and drinks | €265 |
| Local transit | €95 |
| Tickets and day trip entries | €210 |
| Buffer for snacks, taxis, extras | €120 |
| Total planned spend | **€1,210** |

This stays comfortably under your **€1,800** cap, leaving room for a nicer seafood dinner, upgraded lodging, or extra museum entries.

## Best Area to Stay
- **Best fit:** **Baixa/Chiado**
- **Also strong:** **Rossio** or **Avenida da Liberdade**
- Why it works:
  - Safe, central, and well connected
  - Easy walking access to historic neighborhoods
  - Good metro and train links for Sintra and airport transfers
  - Fewer uphill climbs than staying deeper in Alfama

# Packing List for Lisbon in April

- Comfortable walking shoes with good grip
- Light jacket or compact rain shell
- Layered tops and one warmer layer for evenings
- Small daypack
- Reusable water bottle
- Sunglasses and sunscreen
- Phone charger and power bank
- Travel adapter for Portugal/Europe plugs
- Compact umbrella
- Basic medications and blister care
- One slightly nicer outfit for dinners
- Copies of passport and travel bookings
- Small cash reserve plus contactless card
